title: Two Sum II — Sorted Input
description: Given a nondecreasing integer array and a target with exactly one valid pair of distinct positions, return those positions in increasing order using one-based indexing. Use linear time and constant auxiliary space.
constraints: nums is sorted in nondecreasing order
Exactly one pair of distinct indices sums to target

invariants.name: A pair uses two distinct positions
invariants.rule: Maintain two valid distinct candidate positions until the target pair is identified.
invariants.tier1_probe: What information must your state retain to describe a candidate pair of distinct positions?
invariants.tier2_probe: For the verified input, which two distinct positions are available before your search begins?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Candidate state → [identify distinct positions] → [compare candidate] → [justify state transition]

invariants.name: Public positions are one-based
invariants.rule: The returned positions use the public one-based convention, not internal array offsets.
invariants.tier1_probe: Which indexing convention does the output contract use, and does your result obey it?
invariants.tier2_probe: Compare the positions in the expected result with the positions your result names.
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Internal result → [translate using the output contract] → [verify both returned positions]

invariants.name: Ordered input justifies candidate elimination
invariants.rule: Each rejected candidate region must be impossible under sorted order and the target comparison.
invariants.tier1_probe: What does sorted order let you prove about the candidates you discard?
invariants.tier2_probe: At the first state that diverges on this input, which discarded candidate could still satisfy the target?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Current candidates → [compare against target] → [prove one region impossible] → [retain remaining candidates]

invariants.name: Search work grows linearly
invariants.rule: The number of candidate state transitions is bounded by a constant multiple of the array length.
invariants.tier1_probe: How many times can your search reconsider the same positions as the input grows?
invariants.tier2_probe: When the input grows tenfold, what does the measured operation growth imply about repeated work?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Work accounting → [charge each transition to progress] → [bound total transitions by input size]

tier_fallbacks.tier1_probe: What information must your state retain to describe a candidate pair of distinct positions?
tier_fallbacks.tier2_probe: For the verified input, which two distinct positions are available before your search begins?
tier_fallbacks.tier3_scaffold: Candidate state → [identify distinct positions] → [compare candidate] → [justify state transition]
tier_fallbacks.tier4_postmortem: The explicit escape hatch permits the reference implementation. Compare each reference state transition with your own and explain why the documented invariant is maintained.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s whose characters are all distinct. Treat each Python Unicode code point as one character; an empty input has answer zero.
constraints: s may contain letters, digits, spaces, punctuation, and Unicode characters
forbidden_leak_patterns: move left past the previous occurrence

invariants.name: Window state names a contiguous valid substring
invariants.rule: State must identify a contiguous region containing no repeated character and the best length seen.
invariants.tier1_probe: Which substring does your current state describe, and what makes it valid?
invariants.tier2_probe: At the first repeated character on this input, which region does your state still claim is valid?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Current region → [test uniqueness] → [repair state if needed] → [measure valid region]

invariants.name: Stale duplicate locations cannot move the window backward
invariants.rule: Only an earlier occurrence inside the active region can invalidate its uniqueness; its start never retreats.
invariants.tier1_probe: Can an occurrence outside your active region invalidate that region?
invariants.tier2_probe: For this input, is the remembered occurrence still inside the active region when you use it?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Remembered occurrence → [check membership in active region] → [justify boundary transition]

invariants.name: Length and empty input obey the public contract
invariants.rule: The reported length counts all characters in a valid region and is zero for empty input.
invariants.tier1_probe: How does your length calculation behave for an empty region and a one-character region?
invariants.tier2_probe: Count the characters in the shortest valid region shown by this counterexample.
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Region boundaries → [derive inclusive length] → [check empty and singleton cases]

invariants.name: State transitions are amortized linear
invariants.rule: Record enough history to avoid repeatedly rebuilding or rescanning candidate substrings.
invariants.tier1_probe: Which information could prevent your search from rechecking the same characters?
invariants.tier2_probe: What does the measured work growth say about rescanning candidate regions?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: History summary → [bounded per-character transition] → [amortized work bound]

tier_fallbacks.tier1_probe: Which substring does your current state describe, and what makes it valid?
tier_fallbacks.tier2_probe: At the first repeated character on this input, which region does your state still claim is valid?
tier_fallbacks.tier3_scaffold: Current region → [test uniqueness] → [repair state if needed] → [measure valid region]
tier_fallbacks.tier4_postmortem: The explicit escape hatch permits the reference implementation. Compare each reference state transition with your own and explain why the documented invariant is maintained.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: A strictly increasing integer array was rotated at an unknown position, possibly zero positions. Return its smallest value in logarithmic time. Values are distinct; the ties archetype checks coincident search boundaries.
constraints: nums is a rotation of a strictly increasing array
forbidden_leak_patterns: compare the middle value to the rightmost value

invariants.name: Search interval always contains the minimum
invariants.rule: Every retained search interval must contain at least one position of the minimum.
invariants.tier1_probe: What claim does your current search interval make about the minimum?
invariants.tier2_probe: Mark the actual minimum on this input; after which transition does it leave your interval?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Current interval → [identify guaranteed candidate] → [justify retained interval]

invariants.name: Discarded side follows a valid ordering proof
invariants.rule: The comparison must distinguish the ordered regions and never discard a still-possible minimum.
invariants.tier1_probe: Which ordering fact proves that your discarded side cannot contain the minimum?
invariants.tier2_probe: On the shortest failing input, what ordering fact supports your chosen interval update?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Observed ordering → [prove impossible region] → [retain every possible minimum]

invariants.name: The interval shrinks without losing its final candidate
invariants.rule: Each iteration strictly reduces the unresolved interval until a single valid candidate remains.
invariants.tier1_probe: Does every iteration make progress even when your boundaries are adjacent?
invariants.tier2_probe: Trace the boundary positions on this input until they become adjacent; what changes next?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Interval size → [verify strict decrease] → [preserve final candidate] → [check termination]

invariants.name: Search removes a constant fraction of candidates
invariants.rule: The number of inspected candidates must grow logarithmically rather than linearly.
invariants.tier1_probe: What fraction of the candidate interval disappears after one decision?
invariants.tier2_probe: How does the measured tenfold input scaling compare with the required search growth?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Candidate count → [bound remaining fraction per step] → [derive iteration growth]

tier_fallbacks.tier1_probe: What claim does your current search interval make about the minimum?
tier_fallbacks.tier2_probe: Mark the actual minimum on this input; after which transition does it leave your interval?
tier_fallbacks.tier3_scaffold: Current interval → [identify guaranteed candidate] → [justify retained interval]
tier_fallbacks.tier4_postmortem: The explicit escape hatch permits the reference implementation. Compare each reference state transition with your own and explain why the documented invariant is maintained.

title: House Robber — Maximum Non-Adjacent Sum
description: Given the nonnegative value held in each house along a street, return the maximum total obtainable without choosing two adjacent houses. Choosing no house is allowed. Use linear time and constant auxiliary state.
constraints: The first and last houses are not adjacent

invariants.name: State describes a legal prefix optimum
invariants.rule: Each state is the maximum value obtainable from a named prefix while never selecting adjacent houses.
invariants.tier1_probe: Which prefix does each of your state values describe, and what makes its selection legal?
invariants.tier2_probe: For the verified input, which selected houses does your intermediate state represent?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Named prefix → [define legal selections] → [compare choices for the next house] → [retain prefix optimum]

invariants.name: Small prefixes have complete legal optima
invariants.rule: Initialization must handle one-house and two-house prefixes without reading missing positions or selecting adjacent houses together.
invariants.tier1_probe: What legal choices exist when the street contains only one house?
invariants.tier2_probe: Enumerate the legal selections in this shortest input and compare them with your initialized state.
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Smallest prefix → [enumerate legal choices] → [assign matching state] → [check the next prefix]

invariants.name: Taking a house excludes its immediate predecessor
invariants.rule: A transition that selects the current house must combine it only with a compatible earlier prefix; skipping it preserves the previous legal optimum.
invariants.tier1_probe: If a candidate includes the current house, which earlier choices remain compatible with it?
invariants.tier2_probe: In the verified input, does the selection represented by your result contain neighboring houses?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Current house → [separate compatible legal choices] → [compare complete candidates] → [preserve prior state meanings]

invariants.name: Repeated prefix subproblems are summarized
invariants.rule: Process each house a bounded number of times using bounded state instead of repeatedly expanding the same prefix subproblem.
invariants.tier1_probe: How often does your implementation recompute the optimum for the same prefix?
invariants.tier2_probe: What does the measured operation growth reveal about repeated prefix calculations?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Prefix dependency → [retain needed summary] → [bounded update per house] → [bound total work]

tier_fallbacks.tier1_probe: Which prefix does each of your state values describe, and what makes its selection legal?
tier_fallbacks.tier2_probe: For the verified input, which selected houses does your intermediate state represent?
tier_fallbacks.tier3_scaffold: Named prefix → [define legal selections] → [compare choices for the next house] → [retain prefix optimum]
tier_fallbacks.tier4_postmortem: The explicit escape hatch permits the reference implementation. Explain how each retained prefix state obeys the non-adjacency constraint before comparing it with your implementation.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
description: Return the largest sum of any nonempty contiguous subarray of nums. The whole array may be negative; choosing an empty subarray is not allowed.
constraints: The chosen subarray must be nonempty and contiguous
forbidden_leak_patterns: maximum of the current element and
restart the sum at the current element
initialize best to the first element

invariants.name: A candidate is a contiguous nonempty segment
invariants.rule: Track the best valid segment ending at the current position separately from the best seen anywhere.
invariants.tier1_probe: What does each of your running values mean after processing one position?
invariants.tier2_probe: Which nonempty segment does your current state represent on the verified input?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Processed prefix → [state meaning at this position] → [extend or reconsider candidate] → [record global evidence]

invariants.name: All-negative input still has a nonempty optimum
invariants.rule: Initialization and updates must preserve valid nonempty candidates even when every value is negative.
invariants.tier1_probe: What valid subarray does your initial answer represent if every element is negative?
invariants.tier2_probe: Which nonempty choice explains the expected negative result on this counterexample?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Initial candidate → [check nonempty requirement] → [process negative values] → [retain a valid optimum]

invariants.name: Ending-here state differs from global optimum
invariants.rule: A poor prefix must not permanently prevent a later contiguous candidate from becoming optimal.
invariants.tier1_probe: Can the best segment ending here differ from the best segment found earlier?
invariants.tier2_probe: Where does the best segment begin in this input, and what effect should its earlier prefix have?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Prior state → [consider candidates ending here] → [compare with earlier optimum]

invariants.name: Each value requires bounded work
invariants.rule: Avoid enumerating all contiguous subarrays; summarize the processed prefix with bounded state.
invariants.tier1_probe: What repeated subarray work does your implementation perform as the array grows?
invariants.tier2_probe: What does the tenfold input scaling reveal about the number of candidate segments examined?
invariants.tier3_scaffold: Prefix summary → [bounded update per value] → [bound total work]

tier_fallbacks.tier1_probe: What does each of your running values mean after processing one position?
tier_fallbacks.tier2_probe: Which nonempty segment does your current state represent on the verified input?
tier_fallbacks.tier3_scaffold: Processed prefix → [state meaning at this position] → [extend or reconsider candidate] → [record global evidence]
tier_fallbacks.tier4_postmortem: The explicit escape hatch permits the reference implementation. Compare each reference state transition with your own and explain why the documented invariant is maintained.
